`mktemp`: make a file or directory with a unique name.

## Synopsis

<strong>mktemp</strong> \[<strong>-d</strong>\] \[<strong>-p</strong> <em>dir</em>\] \[<strong>-t</strong>\] \[<em>template</em>\]

## Description

<strong>mktemp</strong> makes a new, empty file (or, with <strong>-d</strong>, a directory) with a name nothing else has, and prints its name.

The trailing <strong>X</strong>s of <em>template</em> (there must be at least 3) are replaced by random letters and digits; names are tried until one is free (up to 100 tries). With no <em>template</em>, <strong>tmp.XXXXXXXXXX</strong> is used, in the directory given by <strong>-p</strong>, else in <strong>$TMPDIR</strong> or, if that is not set, <em>/tmp</em>. A <em>template</em> that is given is taken as a path from the current directory, unless <strong>-p</strong> or <strong>-t</strong> names a directory for it.

## Options

<strong>-d</strong>
: Make a directory, not a file.

<strong>-p</strong> <em>dir</em>
: Put a <em>template</em> that has no <strong>/</strong> in <em>dir</em>.

<strong>-t</strong>
: Put a <em>template</em> that has no <strong>/</strong> in <strong>$TMPDIR</strong> or <em>/tmp</em>.

## Exit status

0 on success; 1 on a bad option, too few <strong>X</strong>s, or if nothing could be made.

## Examples

```text
f=$(mktemp)
dir=$(mktemp -d)
mktemp -t build.XXXXXX
```

## Notes

There is no <strong>-u</strong> or <strong>-q</strong>.

## See also

<strong>mkdir</strong>(1), <strong>touch</strong>(1), <strong>rm</strong>(1)
